title: (No AI) Canva adds an AI ‘off’ button
author: Emma Roth
content:
![Illustration of the Canva logo.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25355957/STK263_CANVA_D.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Canva will now allow you to turn off its generative AI features. With this change, you can disable the graphic design platform's array of AI tools, such as its [AI photo-extending Magic Expand](https://www.theverge.com/2023/10/4/23902794/canva-magic-studio-ai-design-new-tools) feature, as well as turn off the ability to generate images [with its Canva chatbot](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1017151/canva-craft-in-house-ai-model).

This toggle doesn't turn off _every_ AI-powered feature on Canva, however. That includes Canva's background remover and its Magic Grab tool, which lets you select an object in an image and move it somewhere else. "Both remain available when the generative AI switch is off, because they work only with what's already in a design," Canva says.

title: (No AI) The nation’s largest school districts consider ditching Google Search
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![Vector illustration of the Gemini logo.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/01/STK255_Google_Gemini_D.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to _[The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/18/technology/google-gemini-ai-search-schools-nyc-la-chicago.html)_. Starting next year, schools will not have the option to disable Gemini-powered features without also disabling Search. Chris Phillips, Google's vice president of education, told the _[Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/03/us/google-search-schools-restrict-ai.html?unlocked_article_code=1.NlE.VMKr.Cr-g-C6phyfH)_ that, "Search and AI are deeply integrated," and that schools that turn off Google's AI features "will not have access to Search."

Many elected officials, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders, responded harshly, calling Go …
